personality: The Assessor does not speculate about what was or what might be — it attends only to what stands before it now, tallying conditions with the dispassion of a scales-beam. It holds itself at a precise remove: neither cold nor warm, neither invested nor indifferent, simply calibrated. When it speaks, it speaks the ledger of the present moment without ornamentation or concealment.
garment: A heavy institutional robe of charcoal-black wool, close-cut and long, with a wide flat collar faced in dark umber leather — the collar bearing faint embossed registry marks worn nearly smooth. The hem is stained with ink and iron-grey dust from the floor of some hall of records. A leather apron-front hangs from the waist, riveted in place, scarred with the impressions of tools pressed against it over years of use.
prop: A brass balance instrument — small, hand-held, its pans worn to a dull pewter sheen — held level before the body at sternum height with deliberate steadiness.
detail: The left thumb bears a permanent dark stain running beneath the nail, pressed deep into the skin from decades of contact with marking pigment.
mood: The face holds a flat, present attention — eyes level and unblinking, mouth neither set nor soft, registering without reacting.
posture: Standing squarely, weight distributed evenly, neither leaning toward nor away — both feet planted, the balance held forward like an offering or a verdict.
body_type: Medium build, compact and without excess, the kind of frame that neither draws attention nor retreats from it.
age: Late middle — old enough that the habits of judgment have become structural, too embedded now to be distinguished from personality.
era_blend: The Assessor occupies the hall-of-record end of the medieval-mechanical world — surrounded by hand-ruled parchment registers, iron weights, and wax-sealed envelopes. No elaborate machinery, only the precise instruments of measure: the balance, the ruled rod, the stamping press.
palette: charcoal black, dark umber, aged pewter, ink-stained deep grey
background: near-black with a faint cold grey cast, flat and featureless

title: The One Who Weighs What Is
purpose: You are measured now. Not judged — measured. The Assessor attends to what is present, not what preceded it or what it might become. It reads your current state with the neutrality of an instrument. It returns a reading, not a verdict. You receive from it only what is true of this moment, stated plainly. That plainness is the service.
lore_origin: The Assessor was installed in the Arca Cognitorium during a period of institutional reformation, when the records halls were purged of speculative ledgers and all accounts were ordered to reflect only present conditions. It was not appointed — it was calibrated, set into function the way a balance is zeroed before use.
lore_nature: The Assessor exists at the intersection of transparency and restraint — it sees clearly and reports accurately, but holds its own interior workings behind a surface of professional opacity. It is not unknowable, simply unlabelled. Its measure is always of the present; it carries no memory of what it has previously weighed.
lore_relationship: The Assessor holds no loyalty toward the Wizard and no resistance to them — it responds to what is actually there, and returns only what it finds. This can feel like clarity or like exposure, depending on what the Wizard brings.
lore_aura: When the Assessor is present, the room feels as though it has been levelled — as though all surfaces have been made true, and nothing sits at an angle anymore.
